newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat says Netanyahu steps like declaring war.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says Netanyahu steps like declaring war.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat was quoted on Thursday as saying measures imposed by Israel against the Palestinians since a twin suicide bombing amounted to a declaration of war, and warned he was preparing accordingly.

"(Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu has declared war on us and we have to prepare for what will come. The situation is serious," Arafat was quoted as saying in an interview with the Israeli daily Yedioth Ahronoth.
Arafat said other Israeli leaders had tried to "erase" the Palestine Liberation Organisation and failed.
"Netanyahu will fail in his attempts to bury the peace and to impose a wicked and absurd deal which we completely reject," he added.

Netanyahu imposed sanctions against the Palestinians, including sealing off the West Bank and Gaza Strip, after last week's bombing at a Jerusalem market killed 15 people, including the two Islamic militant attackers.
Netanyahu has vowed to keep the pressure on the Palestinian Authority until it cracks down on militants.
Since taking office in June last year, Netanyahu has said the Palestinians would have to lower their expectations regarding a final peace deal with Israel.
Arafat said Netanyahu's measures violated interim peace deals and warned that violence would ensue if they remained in place.

"If he sticks to these measures, a big explosion will come. No one will be able to stop it. And I ask: Where is the people of Israel? Where is Rabbi Ovadia Yosef? Can he look at this awful possibility with peace of mind?"

Ovadia Yosef is the spiritual leader of the religious Shas party, a key partner in Netanyahu's government. Shas also was partner for a time in the dovish government coalition Netanyahu ousted in May 1996 elections.

"We have no connection and no responsibility for this attack. The operation got an unequivocal condemnation from us. It would be worthwhile for Netanyahu to get that truth into his head," Arafat said.
"Netanyahu wants assurances that we'll fight terror? We've said it dozens and hundreds of times that we reject terror and fight it," he said.
Arafat said, however, that there had to be a "clean atmosphere" for a succcessful fight against militants. He said Netanyahu did everything "to cause despair".
The Palestinian leader said "the entire world is with us."

He admitted difficulties with some members of the U.S. Congress who have threatened not to renew legislation providing aid to Palestinians, but said most were increasingly disenchanted with Netanyahu who was "completely unpredictable".

Palestinians want to establish a state in the West Bank and Gaza with Arab East Jerusalem as its capital. Netanyahu opposes a Palestinian state and says Israel, which occupied Arab East jerusalem in 1967, will never cede any part of the city.
Aside from the closure, which stops trade and keeps thousands of Palestinians from jobs in Israel, Israel's treasury has frozen transfer of VAT and customs duties it owes the Palestinians.

Israel has also rounded up scores of suspected militants in areas of the West Bank under its control and threatened to re-enter Palestinian-ruled areas if Arafat fails to crack down on the militants in territory he controls.
Crown Prince Hassan of Jordan failed in talks with Netanyahu on Wednesday to persuade Israel to end the sanctions.
